diet.text: Mainly small mammals; also ground birds, frogs and toads

iucn.text: Assessed in 2021 - category not confirmed by SnakeList
iucn.long: The IUCN Red List published a global assessment in 2021 (Turner). Secondary sources disagree on its category (Vulnerable or Near Threatened), and SnakeList could not check the assessment itself, so no category is shown.

overview.text: The Gaboon Viper is a massive, beautifully camouflaged viper of African rainforests. It holds the record for the longest fangs of any snake and is often called the heaviest viper. It spends most of its time lying still on the forest floor, waiting for prey to come close.

identification.text: A very thick-bodied viper whose bold colour pattern gives it excellent camouflage among dead leaves on the forest floor. A pair of small horn-like scales sits between the raised nostrils.

size.label: Typical adults
size.text: Adults usually measure 125 to 155 cm in total length.

size.label: Records
size.text: A 1.8 m specimen weighed 11.3 kg with an empty stomach. A 205 cm snake from Sierra Leone is often quoted as the record, but snakes from that region are now treated as the West African Gaboon Viper. Heavier weights are unverified.

size.label: Fangs
size.text: Its fangs are the longest of any snake: the record is about 5 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Sub-Saharan Africa, mainly in and around its rainforests. West African snakes, once a subspecies of this species, are now listed separately as [[bitis-rhinoceros]].

habitat.text: Rainforest and the woodland around it, mostly at low altitudes, where it lies hidden in leaf litter.

behaviour.text: An ambush hunter: its camouflage is so good that prey walks right past it, and then it lunges and bites.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young after a pregnancy of about seven months, often 30 to 40 babies at once.

diet.text: Mainly small mammals such as rodents, plus ground-living birds (francolins, doves) and frogs and toads.

conservation.label: South Africa
conservation.text: Assessed nationally as Least Concern, because a large part of its small South African range lies inside a protected area (iSimangaliso Wetland Park). This is a regional assessment, not the global one.

similar.text: the West African Gaboon Viper, formerly a subspecies; it has much larger horns on the snout.

funfacts.text: Its fangs, up to about 5 cm long, are the longest of any snake in the world.
